note: Par can mean through or by. Because of is à cause de in many contexts; because is parce que.
Par can mean through in a route; because of rain is normally à cause de la pluie. The source English gloss spans different French constructions.
Par can mean through; à cause de means because of, often with a negative cause.

senses.native: no / not any (after a negated avoir)

senses.target: Pas de problème. J’ai un livre ici.

note: For / in order to; followed by an infinitive for purpose.
Pour may mark a beneficiary or a purpose; a destination may require a different construction.
Pour + noun or infinitive is common; afin de + infinitive is more formal.
Pour is common for purpose; afin de is more formal and precedes an infinitive.

note: Feminine form of professeur.
Professeure is a female teacher; enseignante is another common term.
Professeure refers here to a female teacher.
Both feminine nouns mean female teacher; professeure is common in France and Canada.

Se trouve expresses location; est is also natural. French has no ser/estar split.

senses.native: Server: Hello. What would you both like to drink?

senses.native: Server: And for Nadia, a coffee with soy milk, without cow’s milk.

senses.target: Serveuse : Exactement : un thé nature sans sucre pour vous.
senses.native: Server: Exactly: a plain tea without sugar for you.

senses.target: Serveuse : Nous n’avons plus de lait d’avoine aujourd’hui.
senses.native: Server: We have no oat milk left today.

senses.target: Serveuse : Préférez-vous le lait d’avoine pour le goût ou évitez-vous le lait de vache ?
senses.native: Server: Do you prefer oat milk for the taste, or are you avoiding cow’s milk?

senses.target: Serveuse : Un café au lait de soja vous conviendrait-il au lieu du lait d’avoine ?
senses.native: Server: Would a coffee with soy milk suit you instead of oat milk?

note: French son/sa/ses agrees with the thing possessed, not the possessor; English his/her/your/their requires context.
Sont means 'are' for plural subjects, but French clock time uses il est.
French être has no Spanish ser/estar split; se trouvent specifically signals location.
Te marks a recipient here; yourself is a different reflexive use. It elides to t’ before a vowel.
Te is an object/reflexive pronoun; 'you like' is tu aimes.
Te is the unstressed reflexive/object pronoun; toi-même is emphatic “yourself.”

senses.native: Student: Of course. I would like to introduce Camille, who comes from Lyon.

senses.native: Student: She will coordinate the exchanges with the other groups.

senses.native: Student: Exactly. Camille, would you like to add anything?

senses.native: Student: Ma’am, I would like to introduce Camille, our new project colleague.

senses.target: Élève : Parce qu’elle veut pratiquer la conversation et partager son expérience.
senses.native: Student: Because she wants to practise conversation and share her experience.

Élèves means pupils; étudiants is typical for university students.
